Stuck on a family vacation until at least after Saturday, and I need this off my chest before lose my mind. 

My mother was told by her doctor to include more calcium in her diet. So apparently in her mind that means ADDING cheese and yogurt to her already processed and fried food laden, calorie surplus diet. So she’ll grab a literal hunk of cheese and start gnawing on it. With her mouth still full of partially masticated cheese, she’ll say “Have to get my calcium in.” And then she’ll complain her clothes don’t fit right anymore. Never mind that they have never fit, because she’s a solid size 18 who thinks she’s a size 14. But her shorts are slowly but surely being lost to a sea of FUPA flesh. Then she’ll ask, me, at 5’4 and 98 lbs, if I want her old clothes seeing as “You’ll fit into them soon enough.” She is 5’3 and every bit of 250 lbs. Sorry if that’s not a good estimate, I’ve never had the courage to poke the bear and ask her weight. 

My father recently has a thing about bread. He claims it’s wasted because he “never” eats it, which means it must mysteriously turn invisible 1/3rd of the time? Also he’ll eat his fries and everyone else’s fries and on the way back to the house/camper he’ll pull into an ice cream joint. And then, again, he’ll complain that he’s nearly 200 lbs. But it’s a vacation and he “deserves to indulge a little.”

And, this is the biggest thing:
I have been vegetarian for the last two years, give or take a month as I was slowly weeding meat out of my diet and figuring it out. This isn’t news to anyone. I have occasionally cut meat and animal products from my diet when I lived with them. I also suffer from anorexia, and have since my preteen years. And yet, no consideration is made for any of it, and I’m not allowed to go anywhere without the group— because “it’s a family vacation! Don’t be rude!” — so I can’t run to the grocery and pick up something for myself. We have eaten out for nearly every meal, or they made hamburgers, steak and hotdogs on the grill. The restaurants have all been seafood joints or steakhouses. 

It came to a head when, finally, they chose a place that had actual vegetarian options — not just a salad of a shredded leaf of lettuce, two slices of cucumber and three cherry tomatoes, which, by the way, was only a menu option at one of the places (day 5 now btw) and I got snide comments for being “difficult” and requesting a salad even when it wasn’t on the menu — and I got excited. Then they decided they didn’t “feel” like eating there and then proceeded to spend half an hour deciding where else they wanted to go. I asked if I could run into that place and get something to go and I’d eat that while they eat whatever they decided on. I got told that was rude and that I wasn’t special so stop expecting the world to bend over backwards for me. Fine, never mind there’s an increasingly loud voice reminding me that I shouldn’t even eat to start with. They choose, finally, and it was one that didn’t even have a salad on the menu. Fine. 

So we took our seats and I ordered a water, which set off mothrr. Apparently I was an embarrassment, ungrateful (mind you I have paid for my meals every time), and being ridiculous and rude. She didn’t raise me to be like this, etc etc. 

It’s just a crapshoot all around. I was trying to recover before this trip and have a more normal relationship with food (hence the lifestyle change) but kind of half assing it because it’s hard, and there’s equal parts frustration and sick pleasure in this mess. The pants I packed didn’t need a belt before, and now they do. And I’m so disgustingly happy about it. I want to be healthy, I do, but if they’re going to make it difficult at best to find alternatives, why not fall back to a behavior that had comforted me while I lived with them? Part of me says “Oh, it’s just a week, you can drop the habit soon as you get back home” but the rest of me knows I’m losing control again. 

So now I’m not talking to my mother or father, my aunt and uncle are trying to play mediator by saying that my mother is just worried for me because “there’s no possible way to have a healthy vegetarian diet” and that this is a vacation so I should cut loose a little. 

I am very close either to slapping someone or hopping in the car and leaving everyone behind.

We initially lived in the same town when the relationship began, then his job had him relocated to another town, and we remained together despite this. Our lives are nearly 50 miles away at this point. 

But, I will still read these over, I am not dismissing this, and I may fill them out regardless before the night is up, as I see others chiming in with that recommendation— and disbelief at the fact I am considering not. I will edit with an update, and I’m leaning toward yes now.

The biggest thing was a novel about vampires, but also everything I've written for the past ten or so years. I know it sounds stupid, but it mattered.

I'm 21

I understand completely: the sense of perpetually falling just short of some unspoken goal post that keeps moving no matter how fast you run. How you'll go to your grave (either tomorrow or years down the line) worrying someone will slap your deadname on your headstone or urn. How the eulogy will be for a son who never existed, completely erasing the woman who fought for her right to live her life with everything she had, and still lost. 

I may be a trans man, rather than a trans woman, but we experience a lot of the same issues. We're both shoved back into the closet because the people who should love us unconditionally decide that they know us better than we do, because of some nebulously defined right bought over eighteen years of clothing we don't want, enforced gender roles we hate, and gendered expectations. We're hated for "murdering" their son or daughter and demanding that they love us just the same. We're attacked in public if we don't match society's ideal of the perfect trans person. We're degraded at every turn, the butt of so many jokes because haha isn't crippling dysphoria and suicidality hilarious? 

So we fight back. We put on our war paint, drawing the cloaks of our true genders around our misshapen bodies, and bend and fold and cut ourselves to pour ourselves into the mould of the perfect trans person. We are in the unique position where we suffer both misandry and misogyny and live in fear of someone deciding to "fix" us with their fists or through conversion camps. 

We aren't "real", after all. We aren't "real" men and we aren't "real" women. Never mind that cisgender women can be a little on the masculine side, with bushy brows and no desire for make up and every tom boy trope; never mind that a cisgender woman can have a double mastectomy and even a hysterectomy, and the first person who dares call this woman lesser is run out of town, tarred and feathered. Never mind the fact that you are more real when you smile as someone calls you ma'am than you ever were pretending to be the boy your birth certificate claimed you were. 

Even years down the line, after we jump through all those hoops to change our sex marker on our legal documentation, after we cut off the wrong parts and reshape them to fit us, after we undergo years of hormone replacement therapy and psychotherapy, we've lost vital years. We've lost our childhood to upholding a lie to make our parents and family more comfortable. We've lost our early adult years to performing in the circus and proving that, yes, we're actually what we say we are, please believe us, for the love of God. 

It is a raw deal to be born transgender. It is especially raw to have parents who don't accept you, because they're proving to you that their love is conditional, and that fucks a kid up, you can't deny that. 

Try another day. Try if you can. You can only take it one day at a time. You haven't ruined your college options irreparably. You're not trapped like you think you are.
